title: Throwing a stoneware wine cooler
subtitle: A tall, thick-walled stoneware vessel designed to hold a standard wine bottle at table, pre-chilled with ice
excerpt: A stoneware wine cooler is a large-batch piece: 250 mm tall, 110 mm inner diameter, with walls thick enough to hold cold. It is thrown in two stages , the body and the base , joined at leather-hard. The thickness of the walls and the weight of the piece are part of what makes it effective as a wine cooler. Fired to cone 6.
sourceNotes: Stoneware wine cooler throwing pattern derived from first principles.

glossaryTerms.definition: The stage at which the body and base are joined; both pieces must be at the same moisture level for the join to hold
First firing to cone 06 (approx 1000 degrees C)

content.text: Silica dust is the chronic studio hazard. Silicosis is irreversible. Mix wet whenever possible. Wear a P100 respirator any time raw glaze powders are open. Wet-clean only: no sweeping, no dry sanding indoors. Adequate ventilation when firing. Do not open a hot kiln below 80 degrees C.

A wine cooler at this scale , 250 mm tall and 1.4 kg of clay , exceeds what most beginner wheels can centre in a single mass. The two-part approach divides the work into a manageable body section and a base disc, joined at
. The thick walls mean the fired piece acts as a thermal mass that slows the warming of a chilled bottle.
Wedge 1 kg of smooth stoneware. Centre on the wheel head. This is a large mass , use a medium-low wheel speed and take your time centring.

Open to a 90 mm floor, leaving 10 mm at the base. Do not try to pull to full height in the first pass , this much clay needs four to five pulling passes. After each pass, use the rib to compress the walls and remove throw rings before the next pull.

Target height is 200 mm (the remaining 50 mm of height will come from the base section). The inner diameter should be 110 mm to accept a standard wine bottle. Walls should be 10-12 mm thick , deliberately thick for thermal mass.
Leave the base open , no floor. Measure the outer diameter at the base with calipers for the base-joining step. Wire off and allow to dry to leather-hard.
Wedge 400 g. Throw a flat disc the same outer diameter as the body tube base, 15 mm thick.
both the base of the body tube and the top of the disc. Press together and blend the join with a rib. Allow to dry.
06. Dip-glaze the outside only, using tongs, leaving the inside unglazed. Ice and water will contact the inside , bare stoneware is fine for this. Glaze-fire to cone 6 (1220 degrees C).

rows.problem: Body tube collapsed during throwing , walls too thin
rows.cause: Too much water or pulling too fast with a large clay mass
rows.fix: With 1 kg of clay, slow the wheel to medium. Use less water per pull , re-wet only when the clay drags. Compress the walls with a rib after every pull-pass.

rows.problem: Join between body and base cracked after drying
rows.cause: One piece was drier than the other at joining, causing differential shrinkage
rows.fix: Both pieces must be at matching moisture levels , true leather-hard, not one leather-hard and one nearly bone-dry.
